subject: MedCore v4alpha deployment causing p99 latency spikes and tokenization errors
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@medcore.health>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: Pete Huang <pete.huang@medcore.health>, MedCore SRE <sre@medcore.health>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: sudden latency & tokenization failures after v4alpha push

Aisha —

We just rolled the v4alpha model across our production inference pool at 08:45 PT (per your onboarding runbook). Within ~10 minutes we started seeing p99 jump from ~420ms to 1.6s across our hot routes and an increase in 5xx RPCs. Additionally, about 0.6% of requests are returning tokenization errors (invalid token IDs) for a set of internal prompts used in chart summarization. This is impacting our triage pipeline and causing timeouts into downstream ETL.

Attached: medcore_p99_graphs.png and rpc_error_log_excerpt.txt

Can you confirm whether the v4alpha quant profile was deployed to the region we pinned (us-west-2) and whether there were any kernel selection changes? We need an urgent rollback or mitigation plan.

Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Ops, MedCore Health
samira.k@medcore.health
+1 (415) 555-0199


From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:17:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & tokenization failures after v4alpha push

Samira — thanks for the quick flag. I'm pulling Markus (serving/runtime) and Lauren (CS) in now. We're treating this as a Sev2 until we have a mitigation.

Initial checks:
- I see the v4alpha variant rolled to the us-west-2 cluster at 08:40 PT and the quant profile set to q5_8bit-std.
- No automatic rollback triggered.

Immediate next steps we will take:
1) Markus, can you confirm whether the kernel selection path for v4alpha changed (attention kernels or kvcache layout) and whether short-sequence batching policy was altered? If yes, can we force the previous kernel set and quant profile?
2) Lauren, I want CS on standby for a coordinated rollback window with MedCore if engineering recommends it.

Samira — we'll update within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption.

—Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, Samira Khan <samira.k@medcore.health>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:36:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & tokenization failures after v4alpha push

On Fri, Jun 18, 2027 at 9:17 AM aisha_rahman@redwood.com wrote:
> Samira — thanks for the quick flag. I'm pulling Markus (serving/runtime) and Lauren (CS) in now. We're treating this as a Sev2 until we have a mitigation.

Thanks — dug in and here's what I'm seeing from the runtime side:
- v4alpha included two changes in the deploy bundle: a new quant profile (q5_8bit-std) and a tweak to the attention kernel fallback for short sequences to improve throughput for long-context customers.
- The kernel fallback path introduced an unexpected code path where the runtime attempted to use a different fused attention kernel on Ampere cards; on some host batches this results in poor L2 cache locality which accounts for the p99 bump.
- The tokenization errors are reproducible on our test harness when the model is run with the q5 profile plus the new token-mapper table; looks like an index offset bug during token remapping for a rare char class.

Immediate mitigation options:
A) Hotfix the token remap table and push a patch (risk: needs verification; ETA ~4-6 hours).
B) Force-rollback to the prior model variant (v3.9-prod) and quant profile; this is the fastest path to restore latency/quality (ETA ~25 minutes to orchestrate across pinned pool and validate).
C) Apply a temporary per-customer routing rule to keep MedCore on v3.9 while we debug (ETA ~10 minutes to cut route).

Recommendation: option C (per-customer routing to v3.9) immediately + B as follow-up if C shows any instability. I'll prepare a short action plan and a safe rollback checklist.

Markus Klein
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@medcore.health>, Pete Huang <pete.huang@medcore.health>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:50:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & tokenization failures after v4alpha push

Samira / Pete —

Thanks Markus — we will enact the per-customer routing to keep MedCore on v3.9 immediately. Lauren and I will coordinate the rollback window if you prefer a full revert; otherwise we can leave MedCore on v3.9 until Markus confirms the token remap patch.

Proposed schedule (please confirm):
- 09:55 PT: apply per-customer route to v3.9 (expected <10m).
- 10:10 PT: sanity checks from MedCore (sample set from triage pipeline).
- 10:30 PT: decision point to either keep route or proceed with global rollback.

If you approve, we'll proceed now.

—Aisha
From: Pete Huang <pete.huang@medcore.health>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, Samira Khan <samira.k@medcore.health>
Cc: MedCore SRE <sre@medcore.health>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & tokenization failures after v4alpha push

On Sat, Jun 19, 2027 at 8:40 AM PT we applied the per-customer route and kept MedCore on v3.9 while you investigated. Quick update: p99 is back to baseline, 5xxs dropped to previous levels, and our triage sampling shows the tokenization error count is zero for the v3.9 traffic.

That said, we are escalating internally because we have a scheduled model upgrade cadence and need a formal RCA and a mitigation plan so we can re-run the v4alpha test without risk. Can you provide:
- Short RCA on root cause (kernel selection + token remap index offset)
- Patch timeline for token remap fix
- Post-fix validation checklist and canary rollout plan (we will require a staged rollout across dev->staging->canary with tokenized fuzz tests)
- Any potential SLA credit/mitigation for the 2-hour disruption window (MedCore is a committed Dedicated customer under DC-8932).

Pete Huang
CTO, MedCore Health
